description: The agent's vocabulary for LaTeX — the mathematical typesetting system. Commands, environments, math mode, equation forms, citation forms, sectioning. The substrate needs this to read mathematical research text where the content is in LaTeX source.

concepts.name: latex_command
concepts.definition: A LaTeX directive starting with backslash, e.g. \section, \cite, \sqrt. Takes zero or more arguments in curly braces and zero or more optional arguments in square brackets. The substrate's primary structural marker in LaTeX source.

concepts.name: latex_environment
concepts.definition: A LaTeX construct delimited by \begin{name} ... \end{name}. Carries semantics (equation, theorem, proof, itemize). The substrate's primary block-structure unit.

concepts.name: latex_argument
concepts.definition: An argument to a LaTeX command. Mandatory arguments in curly braces; optional in square brackets. \section[short]{Long title} has one optional and one mandatory.

concepts.name: latex_group
concepts.definition: A scope delimited by curly braces. Restricts the effect of font/style commands. {\bf x} bolds only x.

concepts.name: latex_comment
concepts.definition: Text starting with % to end of line. Ignored by the typesetter; useful provenance for the substrate's adapter (% AUTHOR: Smith).

concepts.name: math_mode
concepts.definition: A LaTeX mode where math notation is set with conventional spacing, italic letters, and access to math commands. Entered via $, \(, $$, \[, or math environments.

concepts.name: text_mode
concepts.definition: Default LaTeX mode for prose. Outside any math delimiters. Different spacing rules and command set than math mode.

concepts.name: inline_math
concepts.definition: Math expression set within a sentence's line, delimited by $...$ or \(...\). Compact, part of the prose flow. The substrate's most common math-detection target.

concepts.name: display_math
concepts.definition: Math expression set on its own line(s), delimited by $$...$$, \[...\], or display environments. The substrate should weight these higher when matching answer text.

concepts.name: equation_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment \begin{equation} ... \end{equation} producing numbered display math. The number serves as a cross-reference target.

concepts.name: equation_star_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment \begin{equation*} ... \end{equation*} — like equation, but unnumbered.

concepts.name: align_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment \begin{align} ... \end{align} for vertically aligned multi-line equations. Uses & for alignment columns and \\ for line breaks.

concepts.name: gather_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment \begin{gather} ... \end{gather} for centered multi-line equations without alignment.

concepts.name: matrix_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX matrix environments: matrix, pmatrix (parens), bmatrix (brackets), vmatrix (single bars), Vmatrix (double bars). Rows separated by \\.

concepts.name: theorem_environment
concepts.definition: User-defined LaTeX environment for theorem-like blocks (theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary). Conventionally set with bold label + italic body.

concepts.name: proof_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment \begin{proof} ... \end{proof} that marks a proof block. Typically ends with a QED symbol (open box).

concepts.name: itemize_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment for bulleted lists. Items marked by \item.

concepts.name: enumerate_environment
concepts.definition: LaTeX environment for numbered lists. Items marked by \item; numbering is automatic.

concepts.name: math_operator
concepts.definition: Math command rendering a named operator — \sum, \prod, \int, \lim, \min, \max, \sup, \inf. These take limits in subscripts and superscripts.

concepts.name: math_function
concepts.definition: Math command rendering a named function — \sin, \cos, \log, \ln, \exp, \det, \dim. Typeset upright (not italic).

concepts.name: math_symbol
concepts.definition: Math command rendering a single symbol — \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \infty, \partial, \nabla, \pm, \mp, \le, \ge, \subset, \in.

concepts.name: subscript_superscript
concepts.definition: Math syntax for sub/superscripts — x_i and x^i for single chars, x_{ij} and x^{abc} for groups. The standard mechanism for indexed quantities.

concepts.name: fraction_command
concepts.definition: Math command \frac{numerator}{denominator} rendering a fraction. The substrate's typical rendering of ratios in answer text.

concepts.name: square_root_command
concepts.definition: Math command \sqrt[n]{body} rendering an n-th root (n optional, defaults to square root).

concepts.name: sectioning_command
concepts.definition: LaTeX commands \section, \subsection, \subsubsection, \paragraph, \subparagraph that define document hierarchy. Mark IMRaD sections.

concepts.name: cite_command
concepts.definition: LaTeX command \cite{key} producing an in-text citation. May take optional pre/post notes \cite[chap.~3]{key}. The substrate's hook for citation extraction.

concepts.name: ref_command
concepts.definition: LaTeX command \ref{label} producing a cross-reference to a numbered element (equation, theorem, figure). Resolves to the element's number.

concepts.name: label_command
concepts.definition: LaTeX command \label{key} attaching a stable identifier to the preceding numbered element. Target of \ref and \eqref.

concepts.name: eqref_command
concepts.definition: LaTeX command \eqref{label} producing a reference to an equation number, formatted with parentheses (e.g., '(3)').

concepts.name: newcommand
concepts.definition: LaTeX command \newcommand{\name}[args]{body} defining a new macro. Extends the command set; the substrate must expand macros to fully interpret the source.

concepts.name: bibitem
concepts.definition: Bibliography entry, often produced by BibTeX. Carries author, title, year, DOI, etc. Target of \cite keys; ground for verifying citations.

concepts.name: math_escape
concepts.definition: Math-mode spacing commands — \,, \;, \!, \quad, \qquad — controlling horizontal spacing in formulas. The substrate may skip these when extracting math content.

rules.name: math_mode_changes_the_meaning_of_letters_and_spacing
if: text occurs within $...$, \(...\), $$...$$, \[...\], or a math environment
then: letters are typeset italic by default
spacing is mathematical (different from text)
the substrate's adapter must interpret the content as math, not prose
rules.why: Mixing math and text interpretation is the most common LaTeX-extraction mistake.

rules.name: an_equation_environment_produces_a_numbered_display_equation
then: the content is rendered as a numbered display equation
the substrate may extract the content as an extracted_equation Concept with its number as cross-reference key
rules.why: Numbered equations are the substrate's most stable cross-reference targets in mathematical writing.

rules.name: an_align_environment_produces_aligned_multiline_equations
then: each line is one equation aligned at the & columns
lines are separated by \\
each line may have its own number (suppressed by \nonumber)
rules.why: Multi-step derivations are common in proofs; align is the standard environment for them.

rules.name: a_cite_command_extracts_to_a_citation_node
then: the substrate's adapter creates a citation reference with the given key
the key resolves to a bibitem if the bibliography is also ingested
rules.why: Citation chains are the path the substrate follows to autonomously expand its knowledge from one paper to another.

rules.name: a_ref_command_resolves_to_the_referenced_element_number
then: the substrate's adapter must look up the label
if found, the reference resolves to the labeled element's number; if not, the reference is unresolved
rules.why: Cross-references encode the document's internal structure; resolving them lets the substrate follow the author's argument.

rules.name: a_theorem_environment_marks_a_substrate_grade_rule_candidate
if: LaTeX source contains \begin{theorem} ... \end{theorem} or similar (lemma, proposition, corollary)
then: the body of the environment is a theorem_statement
the substrate may install the (hypothesis, conclusion) as a Rule node
rules.why: Theorem environments are the cleanest source of formally-stated results in LaTeX research source.

rules.name: a_proof_environment_contains_proof_steps
then: the body is a sequence of proof_steps
the substrate may extract them as inference-chain nodes
rules.why: Proof environments delimit the inference chain supporting a theorem; extracting the steps lets the substrate represent proof structure.

rules.name: a_newcommand_must_be_expanded_to_interpret_uses
then: the substrate's adapter must expand \name to body (with arguments substituted) before interpreting
without expansion, the use is an unknown command
rules.why: Macros are the LaTeX equivalent of variable bindings; failing to expand them produces wrong extractions.

rules.name: sectioning_commands_define_the_document_hierarchy
if: LaTeX source contains sectioning commands (\section, \subsection, etc.)
then: the document's structural hierarchy is given by the sectioning command sequence
the substrate's adapter may create Section nodes from these commands
rules.why: Section structure is what lets the substrate's adapter route content to the right IMRaD section concepts.

rules.name: math_subscript_superscript_indexes_quantities
if: math mode contains x_{...} or x^{...} or x_i x^i
then: the underscore is a subscript; the caret is a superscript
the indexed quantity is conventionally a sequence or a power
rules.why: Indexed quantities are everywhere in research math; recognizing them is necessary to extract formulas the substrate can match against questions.

rules.name: a_dollar_sign_in_text_likely_delimits_inline_math
then: the $ either opens or closes an inline math span (alternates between open and close)
the substrate's adapter should pair them sequentially
rules.why: $..$ is the single most common math delimiter; the substrate's adapter must handle it correctly to extract math content from prose.
